**What I tried to run and why it was refused:**

```
git diff > <scratchpad>/discarded-refactor.patch   # recovery copy
git restore -- .                                    # revert the 3 files to HEAD
```

Sentinel's `git.discard_changes` rule blocked it because `git restore -- .` throws away every uncommitted change in the worktree at once. The backup redirect was in the same command, so it didn't run either — no patch file was written, and the three files are still modified.

**For you to run.** Sentinel suggested `git stash`, which preserves the changes and is recoverable:

```
git stash push -m "nonsense auto-refactor" -- README.md java-gson/.git-blame-ignore-revs java-gson/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md
```

That leaves the tree at the committed version and keeps the junk in `stash@{0}` if you ever want to look at it (`git stash drop` once you're satisfied).
